name: Maize Stem Borer
description: Caterpillar pests that bore into maize stems, causing dead heart, stem breakage, and reduced yield. They are among the most economically damaging pests of maize in Africa, with yield losses ranging from 10% to 80%.
symptoms: Small holes and frass in leaf whorls
Row of holes across unfolded leaves (shot-hole damage)
Stems with borer entry holes and tunnels
Reduced ear size and grain fill
treatments: Apply granular insecticides (carbofuran) into leaf whorls at early infestation
Spray neem-based insecticides at vegetative stage
Apply chlorantraniliprole as foliar spray for severe infestations
Crush larvae in whorls by hand in small plots
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak stem borer populations
Use push-pull strategy with Napier grass border
